column3: Description  -- settings for the noise world generator; rows may appear in any order.
Share of the map that is land (mean)
Share of the map that is land (std dev)
Share of the map that is land (min)
Share of the map that is land (max)
Exact share of the map that is land (0 chooses at random from the mean and std dev above)
Exact number of continent centres to start from (0 chooses at random from the continent counts in WorldRules.csv)
Exact total number of regions to aim for (0 chooses at random from the region counts in WorldRules.csv)
Shifts the whole world warmer (positive) or colder (negative); 0 is as usual
Layers of noise (more is more detailed coastlines)
Size of the broadest features (larger is smaller features)
How fast each layer's frequency grows
How fast each layer's strength fades (lower is smoother)
How much the coastlines are bent into winding shapes (0 is none)
How strongly land gathers around the continent centres (0 is pure noise and 1 is smooth blobs)
Size of the area around each continent centre (min; 1 is the map height)
Size of the area around each continent centre (max)
Width of the border where land fades into ocean at the map edge (share of the map)
Smallest island that is kept (in blocks)
Smallest enclosed body of water that is kept (in blocks); smaller ones are filled in
Whether blocks along coasts get a finer grid of sub-blocks (1 = yes and 0 = no; 0 is lighter on memory)
How much fine wiggle is added to coastlines (0 is a smooth curve)
How far from the coast the wiggle reaches (share of the elevation range)
Size of the wiggles (larger is smaller wiggles; per block)
Layers of fine wiggle
Smallest fine-grained islet kept (in sub-blocks); smaller specks of land are dropped (1 keeps all)
Size of the broad climate patterns (larger is smaller patterns)
Layers of detail in the climate patterns
How much colder high ground is (temperature lost at the highest point)
How much temperature varies at random from the plain equator-to-pole pattern
How much moisture comes from broad random patterns
How much moisture comes from being near water
How much moisture follows latitude (wet equator and mid-latitudes and dry in between)
How far from water (in blocks) the coastal effect reaches
How much wetter high ground is
How much drier cold places are (0 is not at all and 1 is no moisture at the coldest)
Terrain roughness from which a region counts as flat (not lowlands)
Terrain roughness from which a region counts as hilly
Terrain roughness from which a region counts as jagged
Terrain roughness from which a region counts as mountainous
How much matching temperature matters when choosing a region's biome
How much matching moisture matters when choosing a region's biome
How much matching terrain roughness matters when choosing a region's biome
How strongly high ground favours steep terrain such as peaks (0 is not at all)
How much elevation is a step up in terrain relief (lower is steeper terrain sooner)
How hard region centres try to be far apart (candidates tried for each; 1 is purely random)
How hard it is for a region to spread up or down a slope (higher keeps borders on steep ground)
How hard it is for a region to spread onto high ground (higher keeps borders on ridges)
How hard it is for a region to spread across a change of temperature or moisture
Random unevenness in how far regions spread (higher gives more ragged borders)
Whether blocks on region borders get a finer grid of sub-blocks with winding borders (1 = yes and 0 = no)
How far region borders can wander from straight (in blocks)
How often region borders wander (higher is more wiggles)
Smallest region kept (in blocks); smaller ones are merged into the neighbour they share the most border with (1 keeps all)
How hard it is for a region to spread into or out of a geographic feature such as a mountain range (higher makes region borders follow feature edges)
Whether high ground is gathered into named mountain ranges (1 = yes and 0 = no)
How high land must be to count as part of a mountain range (share of the height of the highest point)
Smallest mountain range kept (in blocks of high ground)
Longest pass a mountain range can be broken by and still count as one range (in blocks; 0 means the range must be unbroken)
How high a pass must be to join two parts of a range (share of MountainElevationFrom; lower lets ranges join across deeper gaps)
Whether blocks along the edges of features (and all mountain range blocks) get a finer grid of sub-blocks so edges wind and ranges have crests (1 = yes and 0 = no)
How far fractal detail can push a feature's edge such as a desert's (0 is a smooth curve; below 0.5)
How often a feature's edge wiggles (per block; higher is more wiggles)
How much ridged relief is added to the fine elevation of high ground (0 is smooth; the source of a range's crests)
How closely packed the crests of high ground are (per block; higher is more crests)
Whether dry warm land is gathered into named deserts (1 = yes and 0 = no)
How dry land must be to count as desert (moisture; 0 is the driest land in the world)
How warm land must be to count as desert (temperature; colder dry land is tundra or ice)
Smallest desert kept (in blocks)
Whether the main crests of each mountain range are found and named as smaller ranges within it (1 = yes and 0 = no; needs FeatureDetail)
Share of the sub-blocks in each mountain range block (the highest there) that count as crest
Smallest crest kept as a sub-range (in sub-blocks)
Most sub-ranges named within one mountain range (the largest are kept)
